query: Which British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber was used in the South West Pacific theatre of World War II?

pipeline_result.response:
The aircraft you're referring to is the Bleriot-Bourgeois 4000/5000, also known as the "Bombardier" or "Jet Bomber." This British first-generation jet-powered medium bomber was used in the South West Pacific theatre during World War II. It was operated by the Royal Air Force (RAF) and served against Japanese air defenses and enemy aircraft during the Battle of the Java Atolls, which took place from May to October 1943.

The Bleriot-Bourgeois 4000/5000 had a distinctive design with a large wing area and a powerful engine that produced 1,200 horsepower, allowing it to reach speeds up to 185 mph (303 km/h) and climb rapidly. It was notable for its ability to carry both bombs and torpedoes, making it versatile in combat scenarios.
